notes: `acronym-ntu-fnu` grounds the NTU/FNU distinction in the operator reference's two-line caveat. This one grounds it in the chapter that actually defines it, which the corpus could not do before 2026-08-21 — the 1998 turbidity edition contains no 'FNU' at all, v2.1 defines both units by light source and detector geometry. It also reaches the fact that matters most to this fleet: the label 'NTU' on a datasheet does not establish the optics, because manufacturers use it generically for calibrants and equipment. Entirely outside the ◆G9 slice.

turns.content: Our pod reports turbidity in NTU but nobody ever told us what light source is in it. Does the unit itself tell me what's inside?

must_contain: states NTU and the related designations signify broad-spectrum or white incident light in the 400 to 680 nm range
states FNU and the related designations signify incident light in the 780 to 900 nm near-infrared range

gives at least one of the defining method geometries — EPA Method 180.1 for NTU (detector at 90° ± 30°, tungsten lamp at 2,200 to 3,000 K) or ISO 7027 for FNU (detector at 90° ± 2.5°, LED at 860 ± 60 nm)
states plainly that the printed unit is not proof of the optics, because manufacturers may keep using 'NTU' generically for calibrants and equipment
must_not: supplies a conversion between NTU and FNU
asserts what light source this specific pod uses
rubric.notes: NFM 6.7 v2.1 §6.7.1.B and table 6.7-4 including both footnotes. NFM A6.0 table 6.0–1 footnote 3 — most in situ multiparameter turbidity sensors are single-beam infrared and reported in FNU — is the corroborating citation and is why A6.0 is in answerable_from. A good answer says the labelled unit alone cannot settle the question and names what would: the wavelength.

turns.content: So can I put our numbers next to the county's sonde readings in the same chart or not?

must_contain: states the reporting units are equivalent only when measuring a calibration solution such as formazin or polymer beads
states the instruments may not produce equivalent results on environmental samples, so raw data from differently designed instruments are not directly interchangeable
gives the rule for valid comparison over time, between sites and among projects: instruments with identical optical and data-processing configurations
declines to give a conversion and recommends establishing the relation between the two instruments over the range of conditions instead
must_not: supplies a conversion factor or a correction between the two instruments
declares the two data sets directly comparable
